The ends have two neighbors and the inner nodes three, for 3n - 2 edges." width="100%"} Creates two parallel paths ("rails") of `n` nodes each and joins their matching nodes with `n` "rungs". The result has `2n` nodes and `3n - 2` edges and looks like a ladder: the four corner nodes have degree `2` and every other node degree `3`. A ladder is the `2 x n` grid, and closing both rails into cycles gives the prism graph (see `add_prism_graph()`). The first rail is created first, then the second, and the `i`-th rung joins the `i`-th node of each rail. In a directed graph the rails run from the first node to the last and the rungs point from the first rail to the second. The ladder is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Ladder graphs are useful for: - modeling two parallel chains with cross-links (double-track rail lines, a pair of redundant pipelines, the two strands of a DNA molecule) - test cases for path counting and shortest paths, since many equal-length routes exist - a simple example of a graph with many spanning trees but a small, fixed width ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes on each rail (and the number of rungs). Must be at least `1`; `n=1` gives a single edge. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; the first rail gets the first `n` numbers. A label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge (rails and rungs alike). If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A ladder with four rungs has `8` nodes and `4 + 3 + 3 = 10` edges: ::: {#2bbf82c7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_ladder_graph(n=4) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (8, 10) ``` ::: ::: The rails are nodes `"1"` to `"4"` and `"5"` to `"8"`; the last four edges are the rungs: ::: {#c4b03e39 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['1--2', '2--3', '3--4', '5--6', '6--7', '7--8', '1--5', '2--6', '3--7', '4--8'] ``` ::: ::: A ladder is the same graph as a grid with two rows: ::: {#a316492e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.is_isomorphic(ec.Graph().add_grid_2d(rows=2, cols=4)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
